Every year Apple prepares a new chip for its latest iPhone. However, the A20 Pro chip expected to power the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra this autumn sounds like it could be particularly special. Here are two major upgrades generating significant buzz.

#1: The A20 Pro will be the first iPhone chip built on a 2-nanometer process

You can safely expect Apple to deliver improvements with its next-generation chip. Some years bring bigger leaps than others, and the all-new A20 Pro is expected to be especially notable.

That's because with the A20 Pro, Apple will adopt TSMC's brand-new 2-nanometer manufacturing process to produce the chip.

Moving from the current 3-nanometer process to 2-nanometer means the A20 Pro can deliver more power and run more efficiently within a similar chip footprint.

We see this every time there's a major step forward in process technology. This is why Apple invests years ahead of time to secure access to TSMC's most cutting-edge technology, helping the company maintain its leading edge in the chips powering iPhone, iPad, Mac and more.

We don't yet know which specific areas Apple will focus on improving in the A20 Pro, but thanks to the 2-nanometer process, Apple will have more room than usual for meaningful improvements.

#2: Shift to wafer-level multi-chip module packaging delivers a more significant performance boost

Beyond the gains from the 2-nanometer process, the A20 Pro is also expected to benefit from another unique improvement, driven by an innovative packaging technology called wafer-level multi-chip module.

Here's a detailed explanation from my colleague Marcus:

Apple will, for the first time, adopt wafer-level multi-chip module (WMCM) packaging for its iPhone processors. WMCM allows different components—such as the system-on-chip and DRAM—to be integrated directly at the wafer stage before being cut into individual chips. The technology uses a method that connects the dies without the need for an interposer or substrate, offering benefits in thermal performance and signal integrity. In other words, Apple's next-generation chip won't just be smaller and more power-efficient thanks to the N2 process, but will also be physically closer to the on-device memory, boosting performance for tasks like AI processing and high-end gaming, with the potential to further reduce power consumption.

With WMCM on board, the A20 Pro is expected to be particularly outstanding in AI tasks. That's hardly surprising, given that iOS 27 will be heavily centered around AI.

What improvements are you most hoping to see in the iPhone 18 Pro? Let us know in the comments.
